device.model: Thorlabs camera through the PyMoDAQ pylablib viewer
device.name: Thorlabs camera (pymodaq_plugins_pylablib_camera DAQ_2DViewer_ThorlabsPLL)

facts.text: The repository is a generic PyMoDAQ camera plugin meant to be subclassed for a camera through the pylablib library, and the plugin does not work on its own
The generic viewer handles hardware ROI, hardware binning and frames through a callback
DAQ_2DViewer_ThorlabsPLL enumerates the Thorlabs serial numbers at import with Thorlabs.list_cameras_tlcam()
DAQ_2DViewer_ThorlabsPLL.init_controller opens Thorlabs.ThorlabsTLCamera with the serial number selected in settings['camera_list']
The viewer keeps the pylablib camera controller in self.controller and reads the camera information string from controller.get_device_info()[1]
A change of the exposure setting is written to the controller as param.value()/1000, milliseconds to seconds
exposure reads controller.get_exposure() and writes controller.set_exposure(value)
get_roi returns hstart, hend, vstart, vend, hbin and vbin; the viewer derives the image width and height from the first four values
Some pylablib get_roi calls return only four values instead of six and the viewer then assumes a binning of 1
update_rois calls controller.set_roi with hstart, hend=hstart+width, vstart, vend=vstart+height and the two binning factors
The viewer reads the detector size with controller.get_detector_size() when it clears the ROI
stop calls controller.stop_acquisition() and then controller.clear_acquisition()
close closes the pylablib controller with controller.close()
The viewer's exposure-time setting starts at 1 ms and its binning setting admits [1, 2]; these are UI defaults of the parameter tree, not bounds reported by a camera
